welcome.back: PVJets official motto. For the client, flying private is the default, not an exception. Our job is to make it sustainable on cost, time and service.

welcome.front: Italian company with Swiss excellence at its core
welcome.back: PVJets official identity. Italian service culture + Swiss operational rigour (founders and brokers from top Swiss private aviation institutions).
PVJets Co-Founder, President of Voyage Jets. Signs the company profile welcome message.
European Business Aviation Association — the reference body for European private aviation. Recognises PVJets for excellence and reliability.
National Business Aviation Association — US counterpart of EBAA. NBAA also recognises PVJets.
Manager or decision-maker who uses private aviation as a work tool. Priorities: punctuality, privacy, ability to work in flight.
High Net Worth Individual — private client with high spending power. Flies for leisure, family, occasions. Priorities: comfort, exclusivity, experience.
Ultra High Net Worth Individual — top tier above HNWI. Maximum service expectations, virtually no price sensitivity.
Intermediary that charters aircraft from third-party operators and proposes them to clients, acting as their agent. Does not operate aircraft. PVJets is a broker.
Already-scheduled repositioning flight returning 'empty' — sold at a reduced rate. One of PVJets' six global services.
Private Jet Charter · Empty Legs · Group Charter · Helicopter Transfer · Diplomatic Services · Air Ambulance.
First point of contact. Listens, qualifies, gathers essential info (route, dates, pax, segment) and hands off to broker. Does not directly close the flight.

mission.back: PVJets core value — ability to unlock peak-season slots and hard-to-reach destinations through top-tier partnerships with operators and handlers.
PVJets core value — a single advisor follows the client from booking to landing. No call centre, no ticketing.
PVJets core value — true 24/7 coverage. Someone always answers, including night/weekend/holidays.
PVJets core value — one provider for all six global services (Charter, Empty Legs, Group, Heli, Diplomatic, Air Ambulance). Same advisor for every flight type.
PVJets core value — certified carbon offsets (reforestation, renewable energy, carbon capture) + preference for operators with efficient fleets.
20+ years of industry + global partnership network. When a client asks 'what's the right choice?', PVJets has an answer, not a list of options.
PVJets selects operators that pass IS-BAO, Argus or Wyvern. Zero compromises on safety.
Reliability + transparency + premium service commitment. Keep what you promise, hide neither costs nor limits.
International Standard for Business Aircraft Operations. International safety certification PVJets operators must pass.
Argus International — safety auditing agency. Certifies operators on Gold/Gold Plus/Platinum levels. Standard used by PVJets.
Wyvern Ltd — another safety auditing agency for business aviation. Wyvern Wingman is the top level. Standard used by PVJets.
CO₂ emissions compensation through certified programmes (reforestation, renewable energy, carbon capture). PVJets applies them as standard, not as opt-in.

global-reach.back: Size of the global partner-operator network accessible via PVJets On-Demand Charter.
Europe (operational base) · Americas (NY, LA, Miami, Rio, Buenos Aires) · Global (Dubai, Riyadh, Sydney, Johannesburg, Singapore).
Milan, Paris, Geneva, London, Zurich, Madrid, Vienna, Athens, Mykonos, Ibiza, Mallorca, Innsbruck, Istanbul, Ljubljana, Warsaw.
Already-scheduled repositioning flight (aircraft must return/reach a subsequent destination) sold at a reduced rate. Great option for budget-sensitive clients with date flexibility.
2-3 hours of flight, 6-8 pax, ~3,500 km. Examples: Citation XLS, Learjet 75, Pilatus PC-24, Phenom 300, Learjet 45.
3-4 hours, 7-9 pax, ~4,000 km. Examples: Hawker 750XP/800, Praetor 500, Citation VI, Learjet 60XR.
5-7 hours, 10-12 pax, ~7,400 km. Examples: Challenger 604/850, Legacy 650, Falcon 2000LX, Gulfstream G-IV. Typical for transatlantics.
8h+, 14-16 pax, ~13,000 km. Examples: Falcon 8X, Global 7500, Global Express XRS, G650ER, G700. Intercontinental category.
Mykonos (July), Ibiza (August), Mallorca, Athens/islands. Demand peak → flag 'peak season, verify slot' to broker.
Innsbruck (Alps, ski, December-January), Cortina via VCE/Treviso airport. Winter peak → same 'peak season' template flag.

charter-membership.back: PVJets pay-per-flight model. No commitments, no deposit, real-time pricing, access to 3,600+ aircraft. Default for new clients.
Membership programme for frequent flyers of 6+ months. Deposit-based credit voucher, guaranteed slots, dedicated concierge, exclusive events.
On-Demand pricing model: pay one flight at a time, no pre-payments or subscriptions. Real-time quote for each booking.
PVJets Club pricing model: client deposits an upfront amount that's drawn down per flight. It's a prepayment.
Already-scheduled repositioning flight (aircraft must return/reach next destination) sold at a discount. Excellent option for budget-sensitive clients with date flexibility.
Client who has flown regularly with PVJets for at least 6 months. Prerequisite for invitation to PVJets Club.
PVJets Club exclusive benefit: guaranteed access in high season (Mykonos July, Innsbruck Christmas, etc.). On-Demand is 'subject to slots'.
Club benefit: dedicated 24/7 concierge with priority handling. No dedicated concierge on On-Demand.
Club benefit: premium catering included vs standard catering on On-Demand.
Club benefit: discount on round-trip flights vs full price per leg on On-Demand.
On-Demand: strict cancellation (high penalties). Club: flexible cancellation. One of the most important Club differentiators.
1) Volume: 3+ flights in 3-4 months · 2) Predictability: recurring routes, stable pax · 3) Sensitivity to non-price benefits (concierge, catering, transfer).
On Club: 'available when possible' — if preferred aircraft is unavailable, free upgrade to higher category. On On-Demand: not guaranteed.

fleet.back: 6-8 pax · 2-3h flight · 3,537 km · 800 km/h. Examples: Citation XLS, Learjet 75, Pilatus PC-24, Phenom 300, Learjet 45. Most-used category for medium intra-Europe routes.
7-9 pax · 3-4h flight · 4,074 km · 828 km/h. Examples: Hawker 750XP, Praetor 500, Citation VI, Learjet 60XR, Hawker 800. For extended Europe (Moscow, Marrakech).
8-10 pax · 4-5h flight · 4,708 km · 972 km/h. Examples: Challenger 300, Gulfstream G280, Praetor 600, Citation Latitude, Citation X. Preferred category for many executives.
10-12 pax · 5-7h flight · 7,408 km · 900 km/h. Examples: Challenger 604/850, Legacy 650, Falcon 2000LX, Gulfstream G-IV. Classic transatlantic category.
14-16 pax · 8h+ flight · 13,000 km · 975 km/h. Examples: Falcon 8X, Global 7500, Global Express XRS, G650ER, G700. Top intercontinental category.
20 pax · 6-8h · 10,000 km · 898 km/h. Examples: Lineage 1000, Boeing BBJ, BBJ Max 7, Airbus ACJ 319/320. Converted scheduled aircraft, for large group charter.
Typical Super Light aircraft. 6-8 pax, range ~3,500 km. One of the most frequent choices for Milan-Mykonos / Rome-Marrakech.
Very popular Super Midsize aircraft. 8-10 pax, ~4,700 km, 972 km/h. Wide cabin, excellent for executives.
Heavy Jet aircraft. 10-12 pax, ~7,400 km. Typical transatlantic aircraft, made by Dassault.
Top-of-the-line Ultra Long Range aircraft. 14-16 pax, 13,000 km, 975 km/h. One of the most-requested choices among UHNWIs for non-stop intercontinentals.
Bombardier Ultra Long Range. 14-16 pax, 13,000+ km. Direct competitor of Gulfstream G650ER in the top segment.
Commercial Boeing (e.g. 737) converted into luxury private aircraft. Airliner-format cabin with bespoke configuration. For very large group charter.
Airbus equivalent of BBJ. ACJ 319, ACJ 320 are the most common variants. 20 pax in VIP configuration.
PVJets service for very short routes (Nice-Monaco, Linate-Lugano, private heliports). Models and rates handled case-by-case with broker.

sustainability.back: 1) More efficient next-gen aircraft · 2) Repositioning optimisation via Empty Legs · 3) Certified carbon offset.
Carbon offset programme planting forests to absorb CO₂. One of the three offset streams used by PVJets.
Offset programme financing renewables (solar, wind) to avoid alternative emissions. One of PVJets' three streams.
Direct CO₂ removal technology from atmosphere. More recent, still costly offset stream. One of the three PVJets programmes.
Programmes validated by international standards (Verra/VCS, Gold Standard, CDM) that quantify avoided emissions and prevent double-counting. Key difference from DIY offset.
Verra's Verified Carbon Standard — the most widespread carbon offset certification programme worldwide. Reference standard for project quality.
Offset certification standard with focus on social + environmental impact. Competitor/complement to Verra. One of the industry references.
Aviation biofuel that can reduce lifecycle emissions by up to 80%. Today <1% of global aviation consumption but growing fast. Client who mentions it = sophisticated.
Selling Empty Legs fills already-scheduled repositioning flights. Improves pax-km × emissions ratio without increasing fuel use. Both commercial and sustainable lever.
Pattern: 1) acknowledge the fact · 2) cite PVJets' three levers · 3) DON'T improvise specific numbers · 4) escalate to broker for SAF/programme details.

private-aviation-market.back: Aircraft proprietor (individual, company, fund). Buys the jet, pays maintenance and crew. Doesn't necessarily operate it.
Who operationally manages a jet — crew, maintenance, slots, navigation. Holds the AOC that authorises commercial operation.
Intermediary between client and operator. Doesn't own aircraft, no AOC. Has network and contractual capability. PVJets is a broker.
End client renting a single flight. The one paying for the single trip.
Air Operator Certificate. Regulatory certification authorising an operator to commercially operate aircraft. What distinguishes operator from broker.
Manager/director using private for work. Mid-week flights, multi-leg, time priority, decisions often via assistant. High loyalty if service is impeccable.
High Net Worth Individual — investable assets above ~$1M. Leisure flights, experience priority, present but moderate price sensitivity.
Ultra HNWI — assets above ~$30M. Maximum service expected, virtually no price sensitivity, often via family office.
Asset/lifestyle management structure handling a UHNWI family's wealth. Often the point of contact, not the client themselves. Sophisticated client, rigorous contracts.
Aircraft rental without crew — client provides own pilots. Rare in luxury charter market.
Aircraft rental with crew. Standard model in luxury charter and PVJets On-Demand.
Client buys a fraction of jet (1/16, 1/8, 1/4) and gets annual flight hours. Operators: NetJets, VistaJet, Flexjet. Direct competitor of PVJets Club.
Prepaid model of flight hours at fixed rates (25-100 hours). Operators: Sentient, Wheels Up. Predominantly American model.
Aircraft repositioning flight to bring it to client's requested point. Broker cost, NOT directly billed. Synonym: ferry flight.
Synonym for positioning flight. Same concept, two names.
Fixed-Base Operator. Airport handler: refuelling, hangar, pax reception, customs. Examples: Signature, Universal, ExecuJet.
Takeoff/landing permit in a specific time window. At congested airports (Linate, Heathrow, Innsbruck winter) slots are scarce and priced. PVJets sells the access.
Ground services provided by FBO. Includes refuelling, push-back, customs, pax reception, airport transfer.
Aircraft de-icing before winter takeoff. Significant extra cost at Innsbruck/Salzburg/CDG-Le Bourget in January. Included on Club, not on On-Demand.
Passengers. Industry standard. Used in all broker briefs.

aircraft-types.back: Entry-level category. 4-6 pax, ~2,000-2,500 km range, low hourly cost. Examples: Phenom 100, Citation Mustang, HondaJet, Eclipse 550. Not promoted by PVJets but may appear.
Super Light Jet best-seller. 6-7 pax, ~3,700 km. Direct competitor of Citation XLS. Market leader by hours flown.
Super Light Jet. 6-8 pax, 3,500-3,700 km. Workhorse for any intra-Europe route.
Versatile Super Light Jet. Can land on short or unpaved runways. Ideal for Alpine / rural destination access.
Popular Midsize family. 7-9 pax, ~4,000-4,700 km. Cost/cabin compromise for 3-4h flights.
Embraer family (successor to Legacy 450/500). Praetor 500 = Midsize (4,800 km). Praetor 600 = Super-mid with extended range (7,400 km, encroaches Heavy territory).
Bombardier Super Midsize, segment best-seller. 8-9 pax, 5,700 km. Excellent for Paris-Dubai and similar routes.
Cessna Super Midsize. Tall cabin (stand-up). 8-12 pax. Latitude ~5,300 km, Longitude ~6,500 km.
Dassault Heavy Jet. 10 pax, 7,400-7,700 km. Typical Falcon wide cabin. Preferred on Europe-USA East Coast.
Bombardier Heavy Jet. 10-12 pax, 7,400 km. Excellent cabin configuration, popular in fractional fleets (NetJets).
Heavy Jet with extended range. 13-16 pax, 8,000 km. 'Compact' version of the Gulfstream family.
Top-of-the-line Ultra Long Range. 14-19 pax, 11,000-13,000 km. Milan-Sydney non-stop technically possible on G650ER.
Direct ULR competitor of G650. Global 7500 = 4 cabin zones, ~13,000 km. Highly requested among UHNWIs.
Dassault ULR, distinctive for its 3 engines (extra redundancy in oceanic flight). 12-16 pax, 11,900 km. Typical among European UHNWIs.
Boeing Business Jet — a commercial 737 converted to luxury private configuration. 20+ pax. For very large group charter.
Airbus Corporate Jet — commercial A319/A320 in private VIP configuration. Direct BBJ competitors. 20 pax in luxury cabin.
Reference helicopter for executive transfers (urban, to/from yacht/villa, events). 12-15 pax. Typical model in PVJets heli network.
<1.5h Heli/VLJ · 1.5-3h VLJ-Super Light · 3-4h Midsize · 4-5h Super-mid · 5-7h Heavy · 7-9h Heavy or ULR-stop · 9h+ ULR non-stop.
1-4 any (cost/pax rises) · 5-8 Super Light/Midsize · 9-12 Super-mid/Heavy · 13-16 ULR/extended Heavy · 17+ VIP Airliner.
Pattern: 'Expecting [category] ([1-2 likely models]) — verify [variables: availability / stop vs non-stop / client preference]'.
Super Light: ~20-30% lower hourly cost, agile on regional runways. Midsize: taller cabin (work/rest), more pax, more bags. Frequent decision for 3-4h flights.
Heavy: significantly lower hourly cost, more market availability. ULR: guaranteed non-stop 8h+, multi-zone cabin, range avoiding tech stops.

lead-qualification.back: Assigned → 1st Contact → 2nd Contact → Price Range Sent → Assign to Broker. Linear, never skip.
48-72 hours from Assigned to Assign to Broker. Outbound: 7-10 days.
Urgency, Info completeness, Requester profile, Experience, Budget. Each criterion: 1-3 points. Total 5-15.
13-15 points = HOT (within 1h) · 9-12 = WARM (within 4h) · 5-8 = COLD (within 24h) · <5 = consider archiving.
Email: 30 min · Phone: 15 min · WhatsApp: 15 min. All in business hours. Max attempts: 3-4 in 5-7 days.
D0 first contact · D1 different channel · D2 value-added message · D4 last polite · D7 closing email/archive.
A) Stolen cards · B) Identity theft/Impersonation · C) Money laundering · D) Advance Fee/Social Engineering.
ID document refusal · suspicious domain · incoherent phone · third-party billing · pressure to skip controls · crypto · sanctioned countries · pax never reachable.
Gmail for business · LinkedIn absent/recent · incoherent info · text only (no calls) · unrealistic budget · lots of info but no purchase.
3+ simultaneous CRITICAL red flags = IMMEDIATE escalation. 1-2 = investigate before escalating.
1) ID document · 2) Digital verification (LinkedIn, Google, site) · 3) Voice/video call · 4) Business verification (B2B) · 5) Sanctions screening (OFAC/EU/UN/FATF).
OFAC SDN List (USA) · EU Consolidated Sanctions · UN Security Council · FATF High-Risk Jurisdictions. Tools: OpenSanctions, Sanctions Explorer.
First+last name · valid email · phone+prefix · company/role (B2B) · departure · arrival · dates · pax · trip type · budget · ID document · KYC Light complete.
Request summary · client profile · budget+expectations · KYC status · communication notes · red/yellow flags · interaction history · recommendations.
NEVER say they're under anti-fraud verification. Use 'we are finalising internal checks' or similar. If real fraud → disappears. If real client → you offend them.

lead-qualification.front: When in doubt what do you do?
lead-qualification.back: ESCALATE. Team Lead exists for that. Pause conversation, document in Salesforce, contact Team Lead via internal channel, wait for guidance before proceeding.

whatsapp-communication.back: 15 minutes during business hours (09:00-20:00 CET). Beyond 30 min, conversion drops significantly. HNWI standard.

1) Client sets the pace · 2) Concierge>seller · 3) Every message adds value · 4) Formality is infrastructure · 5) WA isn't email · 6) One question only · 7) Price before PDF · 8) Discretion + audit trail.
'Buongiorno Dott. / Dott.ssa [Surname], sono [Name] di PVJets'. Never 'Ciao', 'Salve', 'Hi'.
'Good morning Mr. / Mrs. [Surname], this is [Name] from PVJets'. Never 'Hi', never 'Hey'.
Package · Super price · Amazing deal · ASAP · Only for VIP · emoji 😊👍✈️ · multiple exclamation marks !!.
Investment · Curated proposal · Bespoke solution · At your entire disposal · At your earliest convenience · Tailored.
'Resto a Sua completa disposizione' · 'Un cordiale saluto, [Nome] — PVJets'. Never 'A presto', 'Ciao', 'Cheers'.
'I remain at your entire disposal' · 'With my kindest regards, [Name] — PVJets'. Never 'Cheers', 'Talk soon'.
SDR is sole point of contact from first message to post-flight. Broker invisible (coordinates internally). For HNWI/UHNWI with single-contact preference, simple/medium requests, high urgency.
WhatsApp group with client + SDR + broker. Broker enters directly with offer. SDR is gatekeeper + retention. For complex requests (multi-leg), high value, curious client.
Always Path A. You can escalate to B later ('let me introduce the senior broker'). The reverse — group to 1:1 — is perceived as loss of attention.
Max 2 options · price in BODY of message (not in PDF) · 24h time format · euro with thousands separator (€ 28,500) · ONE single closing question.
One follow-up only at 4-6h. Light tone, no pressure. Don't repeat the option list: brief reference only.
PVJets SDR doesn't sell: accompanies. No closing pressure. Client perceives care, not urgency. Guiding principle #2.

scenarios.front: The 3 triage questions on incoming request
scenarios.back: 1) Who's writing? (direct client/broker/agency · HNWI/exec/B2B · new/recurring). 2) What do they really want? (essential info · real urgency or tactic · coherence). 3) Are there red flags?
3+ simultaneous CRITICAL red flags = immediate escalation to Team Lead. 1-2 = investigate before escalating. Never overlook red flags.

scenarios.front: What NEVER to promise on first message
scenarios.back: No prices · no guaranteed availability · no specific category · no time commitments. The first reply qualifies and proposes the next step.

scenarios.front: When to propose Path B (group with broker)
scenarios.back: Complex requests (multi-leg, technical needs), high estimated value, curious/available client, cases benefiting from parallel coordination. If in doubt = always Path A.

Volume: 3+ flights in 3-4 months · Predictability: recurring routes, stable pax · Valuing non-price benefits (concierge, transfer, catering). When you see them: flag the broker, don't propose yourself.
'We are finalising internal checks, I'll update you as soon as possible.' Never say 'you're under anti-fraud verification'. Never 'we can't help you'.

scenarios.front: Heavy vs ULR for transatlantic combo
scenarios.back: Rome-NY ~8h: Heavy is enough (Falcon 2000LX, Challenger 605: 7,400 km). ULR (G650ER, Global 7500: 13,000 km) proposed if client wants guaranteed non-stop or superior cabin.
[who]: recurring client / new / referral. [request]: route, dates, pax, type. [aircraft]: expecting Category X (model1/model2). [flag]: candidate Club / peak season / red flags resolved.
1) Formal greeting (Good morning + Mr./Mrs.+Surname) · 2) I+PVJets self-introduction · 3) Acknowledge request · 4) ONE qualifying question · 5) Disposal closing. Max 3-4 lines.
Brand (1-3) + Services/Fleet/ESG (4-6) + Market/Aircraft (7-8) + SDR procedures (9-10) + Practice (11). Everything composes in the first hour with a real client.
